papers_found.title: Exploring Apparel E-Commerce Unethical Return Experience: A Multi-Method Investigation
papers_found.key_finding: Unethical return behavior (wardrobing, opportunistic return fraud) represents 5% to 11% of total e-commerce fashion returns, while the vast majority (89%-95%) of returns are legitimate due to sizing, color mismatch, or fit issues.
papers_found.implication_for_trinetra: High inspection friction applied universally across all returns would alienate honest customers. TriNetra MUST implement Adaptive Verification (low friction for high-trust buyers, elevated friction for high-risk flags).

search_category_1_fraud_rates.summary: Literature indicates that return fraud, while accounting for billions in annual losses globally, affects a minority subset of total orders. Systems must operate adaptively to protect legitimate customer experience.

papers_found.title: Preventing Return Fraud in Reverse Logistics—A Case Study of ESPRES Solution by Ethereum
papers_found.key_finding: Single-source warehouse inspection alone fails to detect origin tampering (e.g. counterfeit swap prior to return pickup). Multi-point evidence (carrier scans + smart contract ownership records) is required to establish chain of custody.
papers_found.implication_for_trinetra: Multi-source evidence fusion is demonstrably superior to single-source inspection for fraud detection, but requires automated evidence consistency checks to handle noisy carrier data.

search_category_2_single_vs_multi.summary: Multi-source approaches outperform single-source methods in detection accuracy, provided data noise and discrepancy algorithms are properly calibrated.

papers_found.title: Blockchain technology for supply chain provenance: increasing trust and transparency
papers_found.key_finding: Cross-organizational data sharing faces severe commercial confidentiality barriers and regulatory compliance constraints (GDPR, data localization). Stakeholders refuse to share unencrypted customer PII or proprietary cost structures.
papers_found.implication_for_trinetra: TriNetra cannot rely on raw central database aggregation. It MUST utilize privacy-preserving cryptographic hashes, zero-knowledge proofs, or localized evidence feature extraction.

search_category_3_data_sharing_risks.summary: Commercial data privacy and regulatory compliance represent major technical barriers to cross-organizational sharing unless zero-knowledge or cryptographic hash exchange is employed.

papers_found.title: E-Commerce Dispute Resolution Prediction
papers_found.key_finding: Information asymmetry between buyer claims ('item missing/damaged') and seller dispatch records cannot be resolved by unverified text claims alone; empirical sensor/video evidence (unboxing proof, weight logs) is required.
papers_found.implication_for_trinetra: Evidence reconciliation must prioritize hard multi-modal proof (scans, weights, unboxing timestamps) over subjective chat claims to successfully close the asymmetry gap.

search_category_4_information_asymmetry.summary: Disputes cannot be resolved by text arguments alone; objective multi-modal evidence reconciliation is essential.

disconfirming_evidence_search.critical_finding: TRINETRA_0550 highlights that cross-organizational data sharing will fail commercially if raw customer PII or internal warehouse data is exposed to third parties.
disconfirming_evidence_search.mitigation_required: Architect TriNetra to exchange only standardized cryptographic evidence fingerprints (hashes, timestamps, digital signatures) and automated trust scores rather than raw PII.
